name: Pole's Card (Karta Polaka)

requirement_groups.name: Polish ancestry (parent, grandparent, or two great-grandparents)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires that the applicant, or at least one parent or grandparent, or two great-grandparents, were of Polish nationality.

Requires at least basic knowledge of Polish, treated as one's native language, plus knowledge and cultivation of Polish traditions and customs, assessed at interview by a consul if no qualifying certificate is held.
requirements.fix_path: Study Polish to at least a basic conversational level and prepare to discuss Polish traditions with the consul.

requirements.blocker_text: Cannot be issued to someone who already holds Polish citizenship or Polish permanent residence.

requirement_groups.name: 3+ years of active engagement with Polish language/culture organisations (no documented ancestry required)

requirements.blocker_text: Alternatively, without documented Polish ancestry, requires a certificate from an authorised Polish or Polish-diaspora organisation confirming at least 3 years of active engagement in Polish-language or Polish-culture activities, or activities on behalf of the Polish national minority.
requirements.fix_path: Engage with a recognised Polish or Polonia organisation for at least 3 years and obtain their certification.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least basic knowledge of Polish, treated as one's native language, plus knowledge and cultivation of Polish traditions and customs.
requirements.fix_path: Study Polish to at least a basic conversational level.

evidence_required.document: Written declaration of belonging to the Polish Nation, signed before a consul or voivode
Documentary proof of Polish ancestry (birth/marriage certificates of ancestors) OR an organisation's 3-year activism certificate
Declaration that neither the applicant nor their ancestors were repatriated from Poland/USSR territories under the 1944-1957 agreements

sources.title: gov.pl (Polish government portal, embassy site) -- Karta Polaka - informacje ogólne
gov.pl / Łódzki Urząd Wojewódzki -- Uznanie za obywatela polskiego, reproducing Art. 30 of the Ustawa o obywatelstwie polskim (2 April 2009) in full
Powroty.gov.pl (official Polish government portal) -- Ubieganie się o polskie obywatelstwo przez posiadaczy Karty Polaka

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, and Poland's single most distinctive route in this build: the Pole's Card is not itself a residence permit -- it confers no right to enter or settle in Poland by itself -- but a holder who then decides to settle can apply directly for permanent residence (zezwolenie na pobyt stały) with ZERO residency-time requirement and the stamp duty fully waived, confirmed identically across five separate voivodeship-office and gov.pl pages (Lubuski, Poznań, Lublin, Podlaski, Powroty). This is categorically different from every other ancestry route built so far in this dataset: Portugal's descent route and CPLP mobility permit both still require a standard residence-then-naturalisation clock, whereas Karta Polaka lets a holder walk in and receive permanent residence on day one. pr_after_months is therefore correctly 0, not a placeholder. CITIZENSHIP TIMELINE, resolved rather than left open: Art. 30(1)(7) of the Ustawa o obywatelstwie polskim z dnia 2 kwietnia 2009 r. -- reproduced verbatim on multiple gov.pl voivodeship-office pages (Łódzki, Pomorski, Lubuski) -- creates a dedicated administrative-recognition track for 'a foreigner continuously resident in Poland for at least 1 year on the basis of permanent residence obtained due to Polish origin or a held Pole's Card,' distinct from and faster than the general 3/10-year tracks that apply to other permanent residents (see pl_naturalisation). Chained with this route's own 0-month PR wait, that gives citizenship_after_months = 12: the fastest non-instant citizenship track found anywhere in this build outside of pl_repatriation's day-one grant. This closes what was previously flagged as an open, unresolved question -- the earlier draft of this file left the figure null rather than guessing; that gap is now closed against a primary statutory citation rather than assumption. The activism-based alternate qualifying group (3+ years with a Polish/Polonia organisation, no ancestry required at all) is a second genuinely distinct qualifying path under the same Card, correctly modeled as OR-logic requirement_groups per the schema's core design decision -- and is itself a notable finding: Poland's ancestry route doesn't strictly require ancestry.
